title: Seafood Paella
kicker: Rice cooked dry in a wide pan, saffron, and the crackled bottom that Valencians revere by name.
story: Paella is not risotto — it is the opposite. The rice never stirs. Bomba rice sits in a shallow pan over heat, drinks a saffron-flecked seafood stock, and forms a crackled, toasty crust on the pan bottom called the socarrat, which is the texture Valencians fight over. No stirring means each grain stays distinct, dry yet saturated, and the pan does something a pot cannot.

The other key is the sofrito — onion, garlic, tomato cooked down slowly until sweet — plus a stock made from shrimp shells, which most recipes treat as optional and which is honestly half the flavor. A real paella pan is wide and thin carbon steel; a wide stainless skillet is a legitimate stand-in. Do not use a deep pot. Paella in a pot is just wet rice with good memories.
fun_fact: The word paella comes from the Valencian word for the pan itself (from Latin patella). The original 'real' paella from Albufera had no seafood at all — rabbit, chicken, snails, and green beans.

ingredients.note: or arborio in a pinch — but bomba drinks 3x its weight without bursting
from shrimp shells + good fish stock, hot
yes, it is a lot, and it is correct

steps.title: Shell stock first
steps.text: Sauté the shrimp shells in oil 3 minutes, cover with the stock, simmer 15 minutes, strain. This pink liquid is paella's soul — skip it and the rice tastes like plain boiled rice wearing a costume.

steps.title: Sear the seafood, in stages
steps.text: Brown calamari in the pan 2 minutes, remove. Sear shrimp 1 minute per side, remove. They finish later; raw-over-rice seafood steams grey and sad.

steps.title: Sofrito, slow
steps.text: In the same pan, cook onion 8 minutes until soft and sweet, add garlic, then grated tomato and paprika. Cook 10 minutes until dark and jammy — this base determines everything.

steps.title: Rice in, stir ONCE
steps.text: Add rice, stir 1 minute to coat — the only stir of its life. Pour in saffron stock, distribute peas, arrange the seafood on top. From here: no stirring, ever, or the socarrat cannot form.

steps.title: Simmer and listen
steps.text: Boil hard 8 minutes, then medium-low 8-10 more until the liquid is absorbed and the rice just peeks above the surface. Now raise the heat 60-90 seconds — you will hear crackling; that is the socarrat forming. Stop when it smells toasty, not burnt.

steps.title: Rest under a cloth
steps.text: Off heat, cover with a clean towel for 5 minutes. Serve the whole pan in the middle of the table with lemon, and claim your socarrat wedge early — it goes fast.

notes: Saffron is expensive but used by the pinch; fake 'safran' powder is dyed turmeric. Buy threads, crush, steep.
No paella pan? The widest stainless skillet you own, max 5 cm deep. Surface area is the feature.
Mussels go in during the last 8 minutes, hinges down, so they open into the rice.

storage: Paella is best within the hour. Refrigerate leftovers up to 2 days; reheat in a covered pan with a splash of stock — the socarrat softens, the flavor remains.

equipment.n: wide as your burner allows - rice in one layer, thin
a spoon you will deliberately not use once the stock goes in
lemon wedges arrive at the end

facts.origin: Valencia, Spain — the coastal cousin of the original
facts.first_recorded: 19th century — rice paddies of the Albufera, cooked over orange-wood fires
facts.name_means: Paella is the Valencian word for the pan itself — from Latin patella. The dish is named after its stage.
facts.technique: Socarrat engineering: one layer, no stirring, listen for crackle
facts.season: Summer — outdoors, ideally with arguments about it
facts.signature: Saffron gold, smoked paprika, the crackled rice floor
facts.serve_at: Straight from the pan, everyone at their own wedge
facts.pour: Albariño, or Cava if there is something to celebrate

relations.cluster_note: Two rice schools that share a border: the north stirs starch in; Valencia leaves it alone until it crackles.

similar.n: Spanish pan logic: shallow, confident, shared from the vessel
